 Bitcoin ETFs lose $2.89B in November as losses deepen 
 By Lawrence Mondal 
 Nov 19, 2026 at 8:00 PM UTC 
 Edited by Olivia Stephanie 
 News 
 The payment rail for your crypto. One card. Every chain. No KYC. Spend with Apple Pay or Google Pay in 180+ countries. 
 Share 
 Link copied 
 U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $2.89 billion in net outflows through Nov. 18, with Bitfinex estimating that Bitcoin has fallen nearly 25% below the funds’ average entry price.
 Summary 
 BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for about 83% of November’s net withdrawals through Nov. 18.
 The funds took in money on just two of the month’s first 13 trading sessions.
 Glassnode’s cost-basis chart weights Bitcoin prices by recorded ETF deposits, giving larger inflow days more influence.
 Bitfinex says investors could sell into a rebound and is looking for several consecutive sessions of inflows.
 Bitfinex said on Nov. 19 that ETF investors sitting on steep losses could use a recovery to cut their positions. The exchange shared a Glassnode chart showing how far Bitcoin had fallen below the average price associated with deposits across the funds.
https://x.com/bitfinex/status/2123454750419042663
 Bitcoin traded around $63,800 on Thursday after dipping near $62,100 the previous day. The move followed a week in which the price fell about 11% from its Nov. 12 close, as earlier coverage reported.
 BlackRock led November’s Bitcoin ETF outflows
 Daily figures from Farside Investors add up to $2.8855 billion in net withdrawals across the first 13 U.S. trading sessions of November. The biggest daily withdrawal was $430.2 million on Nov. 5. Another $411.9 million left on Nov. 6, bringing the combined outflow for those two sessions to $842.1 million.
 BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, or IBIT, recorded nearly $2.40 billion in net withdrawals over the same period. Its redemptions were large enough to outweigh inflows elsewhere on several days. On Nov. 6, for example, Fidelity’s FBTC took in $42.8 million while $403 million flowed out of IBIT.
 That pattern shifted on Nov. 18, when withdrawals spread across seven funds. BlackRock accounted for $148.7 million of the $306.5 million that left that day, while Fidelity lost $69.3 million and Bitwise’s BITB lost $36.6 million. The three funds together accounted for more than four-fifths of the session’s net outflows.

 The ETF entry estimate covers a wider pool of deposits
 The nearly 25% figure gives a broader view than Bitfinex’s estimate for buyers who came in during a stretch of the third-quarter rally. Its Nov. 18 report put the average entry price for flows between Aug. 17 and Sept. 25 at $80,070. That window accounted for $5.76 billion of the quarter’s $6.36 billion in net inflows. At the $64,952 close used in that report, the group was down about 19%.
 Using Thursday’s price of around $63,800, a 25% discount would put the comparison price near $85,000. The calculation gives a sense of the level implied by Bitfinex’s post, which describes the loss in rounded terms. Glassnode’s green line represents the combined funds, with separate lines for BlackRock’s IBIT, Grayscale’s GBTC and Fidelity’s FBTC.
 The Glassnode chart calculates the running average using Bitcoin’s price on days when the funds record net deposits. Days with larger deposits carry more weight, and outflow days leave the average unchanged.
 The estimate describes the price at which Bitcoin flowed into the funds over the period covered by the data. Someone who bought ETF shares on an exchange can have a different entry price, depending on when they traded.
 An investor selling IBIT shares can simply find another buyer on the exchange. Fund assets leave when authorized participants redeem shares in large blocks, reducing the number of shares outstanding. BlackRock’s prospectus says those redemptions can be settled in cash or Bitcoin. The cash route can involve selling Bitcoin, while a redemption settled in Bitcoin transfers coins out of the trust.
 A brief return to inflows gave way to more withdrawals
 The funds’ two positive November sessions brought in $74.6 million on Nov. 4 and $7.9 million on Nov. 16. The second ended a seven-session outflow streak, with IBIT taking in $76.5 million while withdrawals from other funds absorbed most of that demand. Investors then pulled a combined $546.4 million from the funds over the next two sessions.
 Bitfinex’s warning is that investors can sell into a rebound while their positions are still underwater if the move gives them a chance to recover part of the loss. Several sessions of net inflows would give the exchange a stronger sign that new demand is returning.
 The November figures show how quickly a single day of buying can be reversed even when the largest fund brings in fresh money.
 In October research , Glassnode analyst Frederik Theissen pointed to another short-lived test of demand. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $653 million on Oct. 19 after a week of net withdrawals, their largest intake since Sept. 22.
 Trading volume across the funds that day was still below its typical level over the previous year, and their 30-day average volume was less than a quarter of where it stood a year earlier.
